content:
By the time the announcement was made, the mood around Old Trafford had shifted from late-window anxiety to genuine optimism. Supporters had spent the summer wondering whether United would secure the kind of midfielder capable of bringing intensity, discipline and calm authority to the centre of the pitch. In Ugarte, they believe they have found exactly that.

Club sources indicated that Erik ten Hag pushed strongly for the deal, valuing the Uruguayan’s aggression in duels, sharp reading of danger and willingness to do the hard running that allows creative players further forward to thrive. Those qualities were seen as essential as United try to become more compact and reliable after an inconsistent previous campaign.

Ugarte arrives with a reputation already established in Portugal and France, having developed into one of the most combative young midfielders in Europe. Those who have worked with him describe a player with relentless energy, strong character and a serious mentality, traits that appealed to the recruitment team as they sought individuals capable of handling the demands and scrutiny that come with representing United.

There is also a sense inside the club that his arrival adds balance. Casemiro’s experience remains highly valued, yet United were keen to bring in another specialist holding midfielder who could share responsibility and raise the level of competition. With Ugarte available, Ten Hag now has greater flexibility in selection and a stronger platform from which to build.

Senior figures involved in the deal are understood to view the signing as part of a broader rebuild rather than a quick fix. The emphasis has been on younger players with room to grow, but also enough pedigree to contribute immediately. Ugarte fits that profile neatly, and there is hope he can become a central figure in the side for years to come.

For the player himself, the move represents both a step up in visibility and a challenge he appears eager to embrace. His first message was direct, emotional and clearly aimed at supporters who have long demanded greater commitment from those wearing the shirt. If he delivers the intensity he promised, he may quickly become a favourite.

Much, of course, will depend on how quickly he adapts to the speed and pressure of the Premier League. Yet United’s hierarchy believe his mentality gives him every chance. The expectation is not simply that he will shield the defence, but that he will help set a new standard for urgency and resilience across the squad.

As the final hours of the window passed, the transfer was framed internally as one of the most important pieces of the summer. Whether it proves transformative will only be known in the months ahead, but the message from club and player was unmistakable: this is a move made with ambition, and with the intention of restoring United to the highest tier of the game. Any other questions?
